To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) NSF funds a large share of the most prestigious economists in the country; (ii) NSF funds a larger share of the most productive economists in the country than does the National Institutes of Health; (iii) the NSF’s funding of economics is concentrated in a small number of research areas, with the majority of funds going to macroeconomics and labor economics; (iv) there is a strong correlation between the NSF’s funding and the number of citations to economists’ work in economics journals
